patient.history_present_illness: Ms. Chen is a 49-year-old Asian woman with no significant medical history and a father who had a clipped cerebral aneurysm who presents with a sudden onset catastrophic headache that began while she was sitting at her computer at work. She describes the headache as instantaneous, completely out of the blue, unlike any headache she has ever had. Rated 10/10 at onset. She immediately vomited and her coworker called 911. She had no loss of consciousness, no seizure activity. On arrival she has a severe headache, marked neck stiffness, and photophobia. She has no current medical conditions and takes no medications. She is a non-smoker. The positive family history of paternal cerebral aneurysm is highly significant - first-degree relatives of aneurysm patients have a 3-5 fold increased risk. She has never had imaging of her cerebral vasculature despite the family history. The thunderclap onset at rest without any trigger is classic for aneurysmal rupture. Her BP on arrival is 166/94 — likely a stress response to the pain rather than pre-existing hypertension. Overall this is a high-risk presentation of likely aneurysmal SAH in a young woman with significant family history.
